clauses.canonical_clause: Own-target graph and bounded-offset bit-break modulus M(v,b), j in [b,M(v,b)) for every d<=v
clauses.correspondence: Actual definitions printed. No graph replacement, modulus-as-desired-path-bound premise or fixed target unrelated to source.

clauses.canonical_clause: Even d=2e breaks antiperiod e+1, odd d=2e+1 breaks period e+1
clauses.correspondence: Same boolean equality/inequality, indices and parity; no stronger nonperiodicity input.

clauses.correspondence: Strict inequality, v=path0, actual MatchesPrefix retained; clock base/successor definition printed.
Window input for relevant actual v=path0 at every b; no uniform window inferred from aperiodicity alone.

clauses.canonical_clause: Every non-eventually-periodic target admits such modulus using choice
clauses.correspondence: Exists one M for this s, all paths/prefix bounds. Original choice construction retained, no claimed effective modulus recovery algorithm.

clauses.canonical_clause: For every f there exists an f-dependent aperiodic target, no infinite match, strictly increasing starts, finite matching prefixes longer than f at those starts
clauses.correspondence: Exact forallf/existsword ordering and actual source graph P_s. Both no-infinite path and long finite prefixes retained, no single word asserted to beat every function.

scope_limits: No new mathematics or novelty claim
No native Rust modulus/target solver or universal graph recognition
Choice existence distinct from supplied executable local-bit modulus
No word-independent bound for all aperiodic targets
Long finite matching paths do not imply an infinite matching path
